To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the simplicity of the user interface is more crucial than any other feature of the system; (2) the simplicity of a user interface can be maintained even with a sophisticated multimedia information retrieval (IR) system; and (3) this can be achieved by providing multiple levels of sophistication in the interface that can be selected by the user by pressing the same button on the remote control repeatedly.

A layered interface that provides multiple levels of sophistication as a user repeatedly presses the same remote control button can accommodate viewers who require varying degrees of simplicity and power in the same interactive TV system".

the design of an interactive TV interface should be based on a layered approach, where the same button on the viewer's remote control can be used to provide multiple levels of functionality, and that the interface design should be based on an iterative design approach that allows the viewer to gradually learn how to use the system and to gradually increase the complexity of the interface as they become more familiar with it.
